questions.q: You want to tell a new friend your name. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Me llamo means 'my name is' — used to share your own name.

questions.q: You want to know a classmate's name. What do you ask?
questions.explanation: ¿Cómo te llamas? means 'what is your name?'

questions.q: Diego is introducing his friend Marisol to his teacher. What does he say?
questions.explanation: Se llama means 'her name is' — used to talk about someone else's name.

questions.q: You want to ask a new friend where their family is from. What do you ask?
questions.explanation: ¿De dónde eres? means 'where are you from?'

questions.q: Your family has lived in Colombia for generations. How do you answer '¿De dónde eres?'
questions.explanation: Soy de means 'I am from,' followed by the name of a place.

questions.q: You are greeting your friend's mom, whose last name is Torres, for the first time. What is the most polite way to say hello?
questions.explanation: La señora is used before a woman's last name as a respectful, adult title — like 'Mrs.' in English.
